label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
**One star for now: good software, but nobody answers when it breaks**

I'm the director of Bridger Bend Community Library in Montana. We have one branch, two full-time staff, a handful of volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. In June 2026 we signed a three-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud for catalog and circulation at $14,200 a year. Our migration went live October 19.

Since October 28, checkouts have worked only in offline mode, on one laptop. Our holds queue was wiped, and roughly 640 holds are gone. Our support ticket has been open 12 days. We have received three replies, and all three said the issue was "escalated to engineering." We have been given no cause and no timeline.

Here is what that looks like at the front desk. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes to pick up the large-print Westerns he had on hold. We had no record of the hold and had to send him home with nothing. One of our volunteers has been writing checkouts on index cards like it's 1975.

I want to be fair. The software looked good in the demo, and the staff interface is honestly better than our old system. The idea behind the product is sound. The problem is support. During the sales process our rep promised us "a dedicated migration specialist." What we got was a shared inbox.

Our county budget hearing is November 18, and this line item is on the agenda. I would like to be able to tell our commissioners the system works.

To Stackhouse: I am asking for a named person with the authority to fix this to call me this week. The ticket has everything you need to reach me.

To other directors, especially at small libraries: before you sign, get support response times in writing, in the contract. If you are promised a migration specialist, ask for that person's name and get that in writing too. A library our size has no IT department to fall back on when the vendor goes quiet.

One star for now. If Stackhouse fixes this, I will come back and update this review to say so.

Director, Bridger Bend Community Library

---

This comes to about 340 words. Before posting, add your name above the title line, and consider including the ticket number so whoever reads it at Stackhouse can find you quickly.
